Music for Hans Christian Andersen's Tragedy "The Moorish Girl"

history.p: Hans Christian Andersen wrote "Maurerpigen" in the spring of 1840; however, the first night was delayed because Hartmann among other things did not finish the music till 15 October as promised. He did not end-date the score until 13 December, and the premiere eventually took place five days later. At that time Andersen had left Denmark in frustration over the way his drama had been treated.

physDesc.physMedium: Bound in brown leather with marbled sides. Handwritten label pasted on front cover, inscribed: "Maurerpigen / Partitur". Added in pencil: "J.P.E. Hartmann." Written in brown ink. Paper: 16 staves. No title page. In upper right-hand corner of the first music page: (Til "Maurerpigen"). Nos. 1 & 2 paginated together; Nos. 3-5 paginated separately; Nos. 6 & 7 paginated together; Nos. 8 & 9 sporadic paginated. Later pagination in pencil at the bottom of each page. Nos. 1-7 with few corrections (one text correction in H.C. Andersen's hand). In No. 8 later emendations in purple ink, because Hartmann reused the Dance in his incidental music for Chr. K.F. Molbech's play "Dante" (HartW 23). At the end of the music on p. 110 signed and dated: "I:P:E: Hartmann / Op: 33 13/12 40".
